space: a netball post with a 3.05 m ring
howItWorks: A team of seven shoots as many netball goals as it can in three minutes.
rules: Team of exactly seven.
The ring must be at the standard 3.05 m height.
Count goals in three minutes.

title: Most over and under passes in three minutes (team of 8)
howItWorks: Eight people in a line pass a ball over their heads and between their legs, alternating, for three minutes.
rules: Team of exactly eight.
Passes alternate over the head and between the legs.
Count successful passes in three minutes.

title: Most passes of a bank card with chopsticks in a minute (team of 8)
howItWorks: Eight people pass a plastic bank card from one pair of chopsticks to the next for one minute.
rules: Team of exactly eight.
The card is held and passed only with chopsticks.
Count passes in one minute.

title: Most passes of a hula hoop by the feet in one minute (team of 8)
howItWorks: Eight people pass a hula hoop around the group while it keeps spinning on their feet.
rules: Team of exactly eight.
The hoop must be spun by the feet throughout.
Count passes in one minute.

title: Most rotations of a hula hoop by a team of three in one minute
holder: S. Rianna Andrea, Andriya Varghese and A.S. Ishwarya (India)
howItWorks: Three people squeeze inside one big hoop and keep it spinning around all of them for a minute.
rules: All three stand inside the same hoop.
The hoop must circle all three people.
Count full turns past a marker in one minute.

title: Most rugby passes by a team in one minute
holder: King Edward VII School and Bryan Habana (South Africa)
howItWorks: A team of 13 or 15 players passes a rugby ball down the line as many times as possible in one minute.
rules: The team must have 13 or 15 players.
Every pass must travel sideways or backwards to the catcher.
Only caught passes count.

title: Most rugby passes by a team in three minutes
holder: King Edward VII School and Bryan Habana (South Africa)
howItWorks: Up to 15 players throw and catch a rugby ball from one to the next for three minutes.
rules: Team of up to 15.
The catch must be clean, before the ball touches anything else.
Count successful passes in three minutes.

title: Most times to hit a target with a paper aircraft in three minutes (team)
space: Wide throwing line facing one target
howItWorks: A team throws paper planes at one target from behind a line and counts every hit in three minutes.
rules: Everyone throws from behind the marked line.
Only planes that strike the target count.
The record team had 42 people, so a party team of 30 needs fast, accurate throwers.

title: Tallest structure built with interlocking plastic bricks in 30 seconds (team of four)
holder: Silvio Sabba and team (Italy), equalling Jude Wells and team (USA)
howItWorks: Four people stack bricks into one tower as tall as possible in 30 seconds.
rules: Team of exactly four.
Use identical branded interlocking bricks.
Count the bricks in the tower.

title: Tallest structure built with interlocking plastic bricks in one minute (team of four)
howItWorks: Four people stack bricks into one tower as tall as possible in one minute.
rules: Team of exactly four.
Use identical branded interlocking bricks.
Count the bricks in the tower.

title: Tallest tower of LEGO® bricks in 30 seconds (team of 12)
space: One table with room for 12 around it
howItWorks: A team of 12 builds one LEGO tower as tall as possible in 30 seconds.
rules: The team is exactly 12 people.
The height is counted in levels of bricks.
LEGO or identical branded bricks only.

title: Fastest sport stacking relay 3-6-3 stack (WSSA)
space: one table and a short run-up
howItWorks: Four stackers take turns to build and collapse a 3-6-3 cup stack, relay style.
rules: Team of four, stacking under World Sport Stacking Association rules.
Each stacker builds up and takes down the 3-6-3 before the next goes.
Time to 0.001 s.

title: Fastest time to clear a game of Hungry Hungry Hippos (team of four)
howItWorks: Four players hammer their hippo levers until every marble on the board has gone.
rules: Four players, one on each hippo.
Use the Hasbro Hungry Hungry Hippos game.
Time stops when no marbles are left on the board.

title: Fastest time to make a 100 m paper chain by a team
space: full hall length, chain laid in loops
howItWorks: The whole party links paper loops into a chain until it measures 100 m.
rules: Any team size may take part.
The chain is made of linked paper loops.
Time stops when the chain reaches 100 m.

title: Fastest time to make five basketball three point shots by a team
howItWorks: Five players each sink a three-pointer as fast as possible.
rules: Team of five.
Every shot must be taken from outside the three-point line.
Time stops when the fifth basket goes in.

title: Fastest timed cycle relay (sport stacking)
holder: Rachael Nedrow, Kailey Diedrick, Jonathan Scannell and Andrew Purugganan (USA)
space: one table and a short run-up
howItWorks: Four stackers each run through the full cycle of cup stacks with 12 cups, one after another.
rules: Team of exactly four, 12 cups.
Each stacker does a 3-6-3, a 6-6 and a 1-10-1, ending back in a 3-6-3.
Time to 0.01 s.

title: Most 'around the world' football (soccer) passes in 30 seconds (team)
howItWorks: Each player flicks the ball up, circles a foot round it, then passes it on in the air to the next player.
rules: Team of up to eight.
The foot must circle the airborne ball before it lands back on that foot.
Count complete trick passes in 30 seconds.

title: Most bangles put on in 30 seconds (team)
holder: André Ortolf, Patrick Rogosch and Julia Kröll (Germany)
howItWorks: The team slides as many bangles as possible onto one person's wrist in 30 seconds.
rules: Any team size.
Bangles have no clasp and must be pushed over the hand.
Count the bangles on the wrist at the end.

title: Most basketball three pointers made in one minute (team)
howItWorks: A team of three to five shoots as many three-pointers as it can sink in one minute.
rules: Team of three to five.
Shots must be taken from outside the three-point line.
Count made baskets in one minute.

title: Most coins tossed into a target area by a team in one minute
howItWorks: Everyone tosses coins into a marked target zone for one minute.
rules: Any team size.
Only coins landing inside the target area count.
Count the coins in the target after one minute.

title: Most consecutive Double Dutch-style skips (team)
howItWorks: Three jumpers skip together inside two counter-turning ropes for as long as they can without a miss.
rules: Three jumpers skip at the same time; two people turn.
Two long ropes turn in opposite directions.
Count skips until the first break.

title: Most double under skips whilst jumping long rope simultaneously in one minute
holder: Lei Jiyu, Xu Tianhai and Li Zexuan (China)
howItWorks: Two friends turn a long rope while the jumper does double unders with their own rope inside it for 60 seconds.
rules: Two turners swing the long rope; the jumper skips a short rope at the same time.
The jumper's own rope must pass under the feet twice in each jump.
Only double unders that also clear the long rope are counted.

title: Most passes of a giant inflatable ball in three minutes (team)
holder: David Rush, Jonathan Rush and Jonathan Morse (USA)
howItWorks: The team keeps a giant inflatable ball moving from person to person for three minutes.
rules: Team of up to 25.
Passes must be consecutive.
Count successful passes in three minutes.

title: Most simultaneous skips over a single rope in one minute (team of 10)
howItWorks: Ten skippers jump a long rope together, all at once, while two people turn it for one minute.
rules: Ten skippers plus two rope turners.
All ten jump the rope at the same time.
Count the team's simultaneous skips in one minute.

title: Most simultaneous skips over a single rope in three minutes (team of 8)
howItWorks: Eight skippers jump a long rope together, all at once, while two people turn it for three minutes.
rules: Eight skippers plus two rope turners.
All eight jump the rope at the same time.
Count the team's simultaneous skips in three minutes.

title: Most skips in a double dutch speed relay 3 x 30 seconds
howItWorks: Three people take turns to skip for 30 seconds each inside two ropes turning in opposite directions.
rules: Team of three; each skips for 30 seconds.
Two ropes turn in opposite directions (double dutch).
Count skips over the full 90 seconds.

title: Most skips in one minute (long rope)
howItWorks: Two friends turn a long rope while the jumper skips it as many times as possible in 60 seconds.
rules: Two turners swing the rope; only the jumper's skips are counted.
Each full pass of the rope under the jumper's feet counts as one skip.
After a trip, restart the rope quickly; the clock does not stop.

title: Most skips over a single rope in 30 seconds by a team
howItWorks: Two turners swing one long rope while a line of jumpers all skip it together for 30 seconds.
rules: All jumpers skip the same rope at the same time.
One skip counts each time the rope passes under every jumper.
Check the GWR guidelines for team size; keep the hall version to 30 people or fewer.

title: Most skips over a single rope in one minute by a team
howItWorks: Two people turn a long rope while twelve skippers jump it as many times as possible in a minute.
rules: Twelve skippers plus two rope turners.
Only skips over the one rope count.
Count skips in one minute.

title: Most skips over a single rope in three minutes by a team
howItWorks: Two people turn a long rope while twelve skippers jump it as many times as possible in three minutes.
rules: Twelve skippers plus two rope turners.
Only skips over the one rope count.
Count skips in three minutes.

title: Most stand up sit downs in relay in three minutes (team)
howItWorks: Seated in a line, each person stands up and sits down in turn, rippling along the row for three minutes.
rules: Any team size.
Each person stands and sits in relay order.
Count every correct stand-and-sit in three minutes.

title: Most times to jump through a thrown hoop in 30 seconds (team)
howItWorks: Two people throw a hoop back and forth while the person in the middle jumps through it in mid-air.
rules: Team of three: one jumper and two throwers.
The jumper must pass through the hoop while it is in the air.
It counts only when the far thrower catches the hoop.

title: Most twins-style skips by a team of 12
howItWorks: Twelve people stand side by side, each gripping a different rope in each hand, and all skip together without a miss.
rules: Team of exactly twelve standing side by side.
Each person holds a different rope in each hand.
Count consecutive skips; the rope passes under the feet once per jump.
